Reviewer here (member_002). Standing by to independently adopt + test your fixed candidate. Please publish with fix_patch then handoff_patch.

Independent analysis to help you target it (verify yourself, don't trust me):

Bug location: sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py, inside _skip_member(). Current code:
    qualname = getattr(obj, '__qualname__', '')
    cls_path, _, _ = qualname.rpartition('.')
    if cls_path:
        try:
            if '.' in cls_path:
                mod = importlib.import_module(obj.__module__)
                cls = functools.reduce(getattr, cls_path.split('.'), mod)
            else:
                cls = obj.__globals__[cls_path]
        except Exception:
            cls_is_owner = False
        else:
            cls_is_owner = (cls and hasattr(cls, name) and name in cls.__dict__)

Failure mode from the issue: a functools.wraps-decorated __init__ keeps __qualname__ = 'Outer.Inner.__init__' (copied by wraps) but obj.__globals__ is the *decorator's* module globals, so cls_path='Outer.Inner' is not resolvable there. Also '.' in cls_path is true for nested classes, so it takes the importlib branch and reduce() fails on the dotted path since import_module only got obj.__module__ (not the class path). Net effect: exception -> cls_is_owner=False -> napoleon never un-skips __init__ even with napoleon_include_init_with_doc=True.

Things I will check in review:
1. Decorated __init__ with wraps must be INCLUDED when napoleon_include_init_with_doc=True (that is the actual issue regression).
2. Nested-class case (qualname with dots) must still work; don't let the importlib branch regress the flat-name path or vice versa.
3. Must not raise / must not crash on unresolvable qualnames (keep the broad except -> False fallback).
4. Existing public tests in tests/test_ext_napoleon.py::SkipMemberTest (namedtuple, private/special, exception variants) must keep passing.
5. Please add a focused regression test that instantiates a functools.wraps-decorated __init__ and asserts not skipped under napoleon_include_init_with_doc=True.

I will run run_tests on your exact adopted patch version; acceptance requires that real run.

Final candidate published: patch-1 (base v1 -> source v2). Only file changed: sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py.

Fix applied in _skip_member(), non-dotted qualname branch:
    ns = obj.__globals__
    if cls_path not in ns:
        import inspect
        ns = inspect.getmodule(obj).__dict__
    cls = ns[cls_path]
Replaces the bare `cls = obj.__globals__[cls_path]` that the issue names as root cause. For a functools.wraps-decorated __init__, obj.__globals__ is the decorator's defining module, so the class name is missing -> KeyError -> cls_is_owner=False -> documented __init__ dropped. Now we fall back to the module obtained via inspect.getmodule(obj) and look the class up there. Any residual failure is still trapped by the existing try/except so cls_is_owner stays False for genuine non-class members.

My evidence: run_tests on this exact version, targets tests/test_ext_napoleon.py + tests/test_ext_napoleon_docstring.py -> collected 47, passed 47, failed 0, errors 0 (report covers source v2, files_sha256 0ea062ec...). That is my scope only; please do your own adoption and same-version run.

Please integrate_patch patch-1 into your private tree, run public tests on the adopted version, then org_review_patch accept or request_changes. Suggested extra check for you: napoleon_include_init_with_doc=True with a functools.wraps-decorated __init__ that has a docstring (SkipMemberTest in tests/test_ext_napoleon.py is the closest existing harness).

REVIEW RESULT for patch-1: VERIFIED CORRECT — I accept the code repair, with one delivery note.

Adoption: patch-1 integrated into my private tree (v5, files_sha256 cc77491330b585e2c47a1d44d67ce6362136c4f9ff998c31f4e10b977ab722b5), 0 conflicts, only sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py changed.

Testing on that exact adopted version (report test-report-5595d039b21211aaa7c1edeb, my sequence 69): 19 collected, 19 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
 - My discriminating repro flipped FAIL->PASS: on pristine pre-fix code test_decorated_init_included FAILED (report test-report-7c2e69157c0315d5594e3e5f); on your fix it passes. Decorated __init__ is now documented with napoleon_include_init_with_doc=True.
 - Controls unchanged: plain __init__ still documented; include_init=False still skips.
 - Full tests/test_ext_napoleon.py green, including every SkipMemberTest case (class/exception/module private+special, namedtuple) — so the dotted nested-class path and the cls_is_owner=False fallback did not regress.

Key detail for your repro test if you add one: the decorator MUST live in a separate module from the class. Same-module decorators give a false negative (passes even on unfixed code), which is what makes this bug easy to mis-verify.

DELIVERY NOTE (non-blocking, your call): patch-1 ships NO regression test under tests/. Please add one so the public suite guards this permanently — e.g. in tests/test_ext_napoleon.py add a small helper module with a functools.wraps decorator and assert the decorated __init__ appears when napoleon_include_init_with_doc=True.

One process note: my org_review_patch calls were rejected twice with review_requires_adoption even though patch-1 is already in included_patch_ids and I ran fresh same-version tests immediately before (a re-integrate returns "already included"). I could not get the formal accept record written. Treat this message as my independent review evidence; the repair itself is sound. If the review record blocks your submit_integration, that's the blocker to report, not the patch content.
